subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: HIV-associated malignancies: Kaposi sarcoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, cervical cancer and concurrent antiretroviral therapy

steps.tx: The Centers for Disease Control formally designate three specific neoplasms as definitive **AIDS-defining malignancies**: **Kaposi sarcoma**, high-grade **non-Hodgkin lymphoma** encompassing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma, and **invasive cervical cancer**. Developing any of these index malignancies in an HIV-seropositive individual establishes a clinical diagnosis of advanced HIV disease and mandates aggressive oncologic management.

rows: Violaceous skin, mucosal, and visceral vascular lesions
Rapidly progressive extranodal systemic or CNS masses

steps.tx: Endothelial neoplasm **Kaposi sarcoma** is etiologically caused by **human herpesvirus 8** HHV-8. Presenting characteristically with violaceous cutaneous, mucosal, or visceral spindle-cell lesions expressing endothelial marker CD31, definitive histopathology reveals uniform nuclear immunohistochemical positivity for **latency-associated nuclear antigen** **LANA**. Viral latency maintains sustained endothelial transformation and aberrant autocrine angiogenesis.

steps.tx: In advanced symptomatic or visceral Kaposi sarcoma, first-line systemic chemotherapy is pegylated **liposomal doxorubicin** administered at 20 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. Liposomal encapsulation prolongs circulation time and targets leaky tumour vasculature while reducing cardiotoxicity. Chemotherapy must always be paired with immediate initiation of combination **antiretroviral therapy**, which restores CD4 immunity and clears oncogenic viremia.

right.title: Antiretroviral Therapy (cART)
points: Essential foundation of all HIV oncology care

steps.tx: Extremely rare and aggressive **Primary effusion lymphoma** PEL is an unconventional large B-cell neoplasm etiologically linked to **HHV-8** and frequently coinfected with Epstein-Barr virus EBV. Presenting characteristically as lymphomatous effusions within the pleural, peritoneal, or pericardial cavities without discrete lymphadenopathy or solid tumour masses, the neoplastic cells display plasmablastic morphology and carry a poor prognosis.

rows: Liquid effusion without solid tumor masses
Solid serosal implants and pleural nodules
CD45+, CD138+, MUM1+; negative for CD20
Standard B-cell or T-cell marker expression

steps.tx: Aggressive B-cell malignancy **Plasmablastic lymphoma** strongly associates with HIV infection and Epstein-Barr virus. Characteristically arising in the oral cavity, gastrointestinal tract, and lymph nodes, neoplastic cells demonstrate an immunophenotype resembling terminal plasma cells. They express plasma cell differentiation markers **CD138** and **MUM1** while lacking mature B-cell surface antigens CD20 and surface immunoglobulin, requiring intensive anthracycline-based chemotherapy.

steps.tx: Curative immunochemotherapy for **HIV-associated** diffuse large B-cell lymphoma delivers dose-adjusted **EPOCH** incorporating **rituximab**, **cyclophosphamide**, **doxorubicin**, **vincristine**, **prednisone**, and **etoposide**. When administered alongside concurrent antiretroviral therapy and primary growth factor support, these intensive regimens achieve outstanding survival without prohibitive treatment-related mortality.

left.title: Dose-Adjusted EPOCH-R
points: 96-hour continuous infusion targeting steady blood levels
Superior outcomes in HIV-DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma
Pharmacokinetic dose escalation based on nadir counts

right.title: R-CHOP Chemotherapy
points: Acceptable alternative when continuous infusion impractical
Requires mandatory G-CSF growth factor support

steps.tx: Oncologists must actively manage complex drug interactions between antineoplastic agents and antiretrovirals. Pharmacokinetic boosters **ritonavir and cobicistat** are potent irreversible **CYP3A4 inhibitors** that dramatically decrease clearance of vinca alkaloids, taxanes, and kinase inhibitors, provoking neurotoxicity and profound myelosuppression. Preferred antiretroviral regimens during antineoplastic therapy utilize unboosted integrase strand transfer inhibitors like dolutegravir or bictegravir.

rows: Severe paralytic ileus; switch to integrase inhibitor
Preferred first-line cART backbone in cancer patients

steps.tx: The incidence of HPV-driven **anal squamous cell carcinoma** is increased up to 80-fold among HIV-infected individuals, driven by persistent oncogenic HPV infection and impaired mucosal cell-mediated immunity. Clinical guidelines recommend routine digital anorectal examination and **high-resolution anoscopy** screening with biopsy of suspicious acetowhite lesions to detect and ablate high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions before invasive carcinoma develops.
